title: Hollow Fiber Bioreactors for In Vivo-like Mammalian Tissue Culture
protocol: Manufacture fibers by phase inversion spin casting.
Use a non-biodegradable proprietary polymer with NMP as the solvent and H2O as the non-solvent.
Cut fibers to a length of 75 mm.
Insert three fibers into each module, leaving approximately 7 mm excess length at each end.
Siliconize modules before first use by coating the inner surface with Sigmacote.
Allow coated modules to dry in a fume hood.
Autoclave siliconized modules at 121 °C for 20 minutes under 1 atm pressure.
Place approximately 0.5 ml of silicone glue into a weighing boat.
Use a P200 pipette tip to pick up a small amount of silicone and work it into the ends of the module around the fibers to form a 3-5 mm plug.
Allow the plug to dry for more than 3 hours.
Using a scalpel, cut the silicone flush with the glass module ends.
Wrap a small amount (~4 layers) of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tape around one side port.
Autoclave all autoclavable components prior to set-up.
Place 10 ml of 70% ethanol into the reservoir bottle and set up the reservoir bottle, Q-series cap, feed tube, pump, and pump tubing as shown in Figure 4.
Loosely place an end cap over the PTFE-taped side port.
Slide the ends of the L/S16 module connectors over the module ends and free side port.
Connect a 40 mm section of L/S13 tubing to the module connector nearest the capped side port as shown in Figure 2B.
Connect the module to the pump tubing, ensuring that the module is oriented so the capped side port is nearest the pump.
Connect the permeate line and retentate line to the module connectors.
Attach the L/S14 of the Y-connector on the reservoir bottle.
Pump ethanol through the module at 800 µl/hr (267 µl/hr per fiber) for more than 30 minutes.
Turn off the pump and drain the tubing by detaching the pump tubing from the module adaptor tubing.
Drain the ethanol out of the fibers and retentate line back into the reservoir bottle.
Remove the side port end cap to drain the ethanol from the module itself and permeate line, then reattach the side port end cap.
Reverse the flow of media on the pump to drain the pump tubing and feed line of ethanol.
Turn off the pump and reattach the pump tubing to the module adaptor.
Unscrew the ethanol bottle and replace it with a 10 ml bottle containing cell growth medium without serum.
Pump the medium through the system at 800 µl/hr until the retentate line is full of media.
Clamp the retentate line to force permeation of the media through the fibers to wash the module.
Wash for approximately 2 hours.
Prepare a single cell suspension by trypsinization according to established protocols for the desired cell type.
Seed cells in the bioreactor at a density that is empirically determined for the specific cell type.
Permeate the module with growth media if an extensive pre-culture period is required.
Wash the cells by adding 10 ml phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 3 ml of 0.05% trypsin ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) to cover the cells.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 5 min.
Harvest cells in 7 ml growth media supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Mix well.
Add 10 µl of cell suspension to the chamber of a hemocytometer and count the cells.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 min to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cells at 4x106/ml in growth media supplemented as required for the desired cell type.
Turn off the pump.
Drain the feed tube and module.
Attach pre-sterilized end caps (in 70% ethanol) to the module, leaving one side port free.
Transfer ~500 µl of the cell suspension (2x106 cells) to the module using an 18 G needle and 1 ml syringe, avoiding bubble formation and damage to fibers.
Cap the side port using an end cap.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 2-4 hr with manual turning of the module by 180° every 5 min.
Alternatively, attach modules to a tube rotator with an intermittent mixing setting.
Attach an end cap onto a pre-sterilized injection port and attach this to the PTFE-taped side port.
Remove the other side port end cap.
Inject air into the attached injection port using a 27 G needle and 1 ml syringe to drain cells slowly.
Replace the injection port with an end cap.
Fill the module with media using the free side port and an 18 G needle with a 1 ml syringe.
Remove the module end caps and attach the module to the tubing using the module connectors.
Replace the wash media bottle with one containing 50 ml growth media and supplements.
Pump the growth media through the system at 800 µl/hr.
Grow cells on fibers for up to 7 days in a humidified incubator set at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Sterilize injection ports before sampling by holding an ethanol-soaked blue roll against the port for >30 sec.
Insert a scalpel/micro knife blade between the glass and silicone of the module.
Cut away the silicone from the glass at both ends of the module using the blade.
Hook out the silicone plug containing fibers from one end and gently pull to ensure fiber removal.
After excision, dip the fibers into PBS to wash and cut them into a 1.5 ml tube containing 0.5 ml Tris EDTA (TE) buffer.
Subject this to two freeze-thaw cycles in a -80 °C freezer.
Measure the DNA content using PicoGreen and determine cell numbers by comparing this value to a standard curve made with the desired cell type.
After excision, dip the fibers into PBS to wash and cut them into a 1.5 ml tube containing 500 μl of 0.05% trypsin EDTA.
Incubate at 37 °C for 10 min.
Mix and add 10 μl of cell suspension to 10 μl trypan blue.
Load 10 μl onto a haemocytometer and count the number of dead (blue) and alive cells.
Dip the fibers into PBS to wash.
Cut the fibers into smaller lengths using scissors in a 24-well plate.
Add 400 μl of 4% paraformaldehyde (in PBS) and incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Wash with PBS by pipetting 400 μl on and off, repeating the step with fresh PBS.
Add 400 μl of DAPI diluted in PBS to approximately 100 ng/ml and incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes while protecting from light.
Wash with PBS twice as described previously and once with H2O.
Add a fluorescence mounting medium to cover the fiber and image immediately to collect data before samples dry (DAPI ex/em; 359/461 nm).
Take images at different focal planes.
Use focus stacking software, such as the stack focuser plugin for ImageJ, to make a composite image showing an expanded depth of field.
Seed cells (HepG2/C3A) onto 2D tissue culture plastic at a density of 10,667/cm² and grow for 6 days.
Seed HFBs as described in Section 4 and grow for 6 days.
Change the culture media to serum-free Williams E media supplemented with 1x glutamine and 1x penicillin/streptomycin after the proliferation period.
Drain the tubing and HFB module following the steps set out in 3.4.1.
Unscrew the reservoir bottle and replace it with a bottle containing Williams E media.
Pump the new media through the HFB at 800 µl/hr for 24 hours.
Take media samples after 24 hours.
Dilute media samples 1 in 10 to 1 in 40 before use in order to bring albumin concentrations within the range of the standard curve.
Quantify secreted albumin by ELISA according to the manufacturer's instructions.
